_meta.note: Summarised general extension knowledge used only to drive the prototype rules. Condition windows are indicative. Always confirm field diagnoses with a local agriculture officer / KVK. Replace with the verified Kisan Drishti disease dataset.

items.name: Yellow (stripe) rust
symptoms: Yellow powdery pustules arranged in stripes along leaf veins
Often starts in patches, on lower or middle leaves
Yellow powder rubs off on fingers or cloth
items.favourable: Cool weather (roughly 10–15 °C) with high humidity, dew, fog or light rain.
prevention: Grow varieties recommended as rust-resistant for your region
Avoid excess nitrogen, which makes the canopy more susceptible
Scout regularly from tillering onward, especially after foggy spells
nextSteps: Walk the field in a W-pattern and check 20+ plants for striped pustules
Mark and photograph affected patches to track spread
Report confirmed patches to your local agriculture officer / KVK for approved control options (organic certification may restrict inputs)

items.name: Leaf (brown) rust
symptoms: Small, round orange-brown pustules scattered on the upper leaf surface
Pustules are not arranged in stripes
items.favourable: Moderate temperatures (roughly 15–25 °C) with several hours of leaf wetness.
prevention: Use resistant varieties and timely sowing
Remove volunteer wheat plants that carry the fungus between seasons
nextSteps: Check flag and upper leaves for scattered orange-brown pustules
Record the share of plants affected
Consult your local agriculture officer / KVK before any treatment

items.name: Powdery mildew
symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on leaves and stems
Patches may turn greyish-brown with age
More common in dense, shaded canopy
items.favourable: Mild temperatures (roughly 15–22 °C), high humidity and dense crop canopy; free water not required.
prevention: Avoid very dense sowing and excess nitrogen
Improve air movement in the canopy
nextSteps: Inspect lower leaves in dense patches
Track whether patches spread to upper leaves
Seek local expert advice before any treatment

items.name: Aphids
symptoms: Clusters of small green/dark insects on leaves and ears
Curling or yellowing of young leaves
items.favourable: Cool, cloudy and humid weather; populations often build up in mid to late winter.
prevention: Conserve natural enemies such as ladybird beetles — avoid broad-spectrum sprays
Avoid excess nitrogen, which favours aphid build-up
nextSteps: Count aphids on 10 tillers at several spots in the field
Check for ladybird beetles and other natural enemies
Ask your local expert about economic threshold levels before acting

items.name: Rice blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped leaf spots with grey centres
Neck of panicle may turn dark and break
items.favourable: Warm, humid weather with long dew periods and excess nitrogen.
nextSteps: Consult your local agriculture officer / KVK

items.name: Late blight
symptoms: White growth under leaves in humid mornings
items.favourable: Cool (10–20 °C), cloudy, very humid or drizzly weather.
prevention: Remove volunteer plants and cull piles
nextSteps: Consult your local agriculture officer / KVK
